Proximity is expressed qualitatively rather than as a single number; configurations can involve rays or bodily conjunctions; bodily passages require same side of ecliptic latitude. Relative precedence matters.

original_primary_sources.scope: Editor reports anonymous commentator (Wolf p51) maximum distance 15 degrees; also reports Ashmand's substantially different individual planetary orbs. These are HISTORICAL COMMENTARY, not numbers supplied by Ptolemy.

engineering_choices: Four external non-Mercury nonluminary planetary candidates (Venus/Mars/Jupiter/Saturn) are screened, whereas Mercury self-governance and other source routes remain UNASSESSED.

Both Mercury and Moon must have a traditional aspect with the same candidate at the given UTC sample; the original III.13 character-governing procedure is not asserted to require this for every character.
Angular proximity 1,3,5,10,15 degrees for BOTH contacts; no number is source-endorsed. One threshold (15°) is mentioned by anonymous commentator via Robbins but remains commentary not Ptolemy.
Nonconjunction aspects provide conservative geometry with no need for ecliptic side; conjunction-inclusive broader scope remains unverified until latitude check.

Moon motion toward/away exact aspect is estimated by neighboring 15-minute source samples; first and last sample of each of 36 original source shards abstain, and near-horizon sect excludes 5,049 samples.
A single sample can have more than one configured candidate, so applying and separating case counts can overlap.
The uniform UTC 1926–2026 sample count cannot be treated as a representative birth-time or personality frequency.
